content.explanation.0: Why: The gap is followed by a noun (presentation) that belongs to the speaker, so the possessive relative pronoun “whose” is needed; “who” and “whom” cannot come directly before a noun like this.
content.stem: 101.The keynote speaker, _____ presentation on sustainable packaging drew the largest crowd of the conference, has been invited back next year.

content.explanation.0: Why: The two clauses contrast (late delivery vs. launch on schedule), so the concessive conjunction “Although” fits; “Because” would wrongly present the delay as the reason for the on-time launch.
content.stem: 102._____ the fabric shipment arrived two days late, the boutique was still able to launch its autumn collection on schedule.

content.explanation.0: Why: People who feel an emotion are described with the -ed participle, so “pleased” is correct; “pleasing” describes the thing that causes the feeling.
content.stem: 103.Passengers were _____ to learn that the new express rail service would reduce their travel time by almost half.

content.explanation.0: Why: After “to” in “asked … to ___ the layout”, a base-form verb that takes an object is required, so “finalize” is correct; the other choices are an adjective, an adverb and a noun.
content.stem: 104.Ms. Okafor has asked the design team to _____ the brochure layout before it is sent to the printer on Thursday.

content.explanation.0: Why: The sentence presents two alternative ways to pay, so “or” is correct; “nor” requires a negative such as “neither”, and “but” and “so” do not express alternatives.
content.stem: 105.Visitors may pay for parking at the machine next to the main entrance _____ through the Harbor Mall mobile application.

content.explanation.0: Why: The subject is the singular noun “list” (not “suppliers”), so the singular verb “is” is needed; “are” is the trap that agrees with the nearer plural noun.
content.stem: 106.The list of approved suppliers _____ updated every quarter by the purchasing department and posted on the company intranet.

content.explanation.0: Why: The pair is joined by “and”, which goes with “both”; “either” pairs with “or” and “neither” with “nor”.
content.stem: 107.Applicants for the regional sales manager position must submit _____ a cover letter and two letters of reference by March 15.

content.explanation.0: Why: Inspections do not conduct anything; they are conducted by an engineer, so the passive “be conducted” is required after “must”.
content.stem: 108.All safety inspections at the Dunmore Bridge construction site must _____ by a certified structural engineer.

content.explanation.0: Why: After “to” (and the adverb “significantly”) a verb taking the object “the time” is needed, so “shorten” is correct.
content.stem: 109.The latest software update is expected to significantly _____ the time needed to process customer refund requests.

content.explanation.0: Why: Only a possessive adjective can come before “own flights”, so “his” is correct; “himself” is a reflexive pronoun and cannot modify a noun.
content.stem: 110.Mr. Delgado usually prefers to book _____ own flights rather than use the travel agency recommended by the company.

content.explanation.0: Why: The verb “agree” is followed by a to-infinitive, so “to reduce” is correct; “agreed reducing” is ungrammatical.
content.stem: 111.The hotel manager agreed _____ the conference room rental fee for groups of more than fifty guests.

content.explanation.0: Why: The noun “employee” is singular and the verb is “attends”, so “Every” is needed; “All”, “Most” and “Several” require a plural noun.
content.stem: 112._____ employee who attends Friday’s data security workshop will receive a certificate of completion from the IT department.

content.explanation.0: Why: Companies receive “approval” from regulators before selling a product; “approach” looks similar but does not make sense here.
content.stem: 113.Varentis Pharmaceuticals has received _____ from national regulators to begin selling its new allergy medication next spring.

content.explanation.0: Why: After the adjective “careful” a noun is needed, and the fixed expression is “attention to detail”.
content.stem: 114.The marketing director praised the event team for its careful _____ to detail during the product launch in Seoul.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Shortly after” means “soon after” and is a common collocation; “nearly after” and “closely after” are not idiomatic here.
content.stem: 115.Tickets for the Milan Designers’ Showcase sold out _____ after they became available on the event’s Web site.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Between” is used with two things joined by “and” (the cafeteria and the mail room); “among” is used for three or more.
content.stem: 116.The new staff lounge is located _____ the cafeteria and the mail room on the second floor of the building.

content.explanation.0: Why: The main clause uses “will be completed”, so this is a first conditional and the if-clause takes the simple present “delivers”.
content.stem: 117.If the contractor _____ the flooring materials by Friday, the renovation of the showroom will be completed on time.

content.explanation.0: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “was received”, so “enthusiastically” is correct.
content.stem: 118.Ms. Petrova’s proposal to open a second warehouse was _____ received by the board, which approved it without changes.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Since + past point” describes a period continuing up to now, so the present perfect “has managed” is required.
content.stem: 119.Since joining Carrow Engineering in 2019, Mr. Tanaka _____ three major bridge projects in the region.

content.explanation.0: Why: The snowfall is the cause of the delays, so “Due to” fits; “In spite of” expresses the opposite relationship.
content.stem: 120._____ heavy snowfall, all afternoon flights from Oslo to Helsinki have been delayed by at least two hours.

content.explanation.0: Why: Only a degree adverb such as "considerably" (or much, far) can strengthen a comparative like "more spacious"; "very more" and "too more" are ungrammatical, and "such" needs a noun phrase ("such spacious rooms").
content.stem: 121.The newly renovated Harbor Hotel offers _____ more spacious guest rooms than any other hotel in the downtown area.

content.explanation.0: Why: You “review” a document; “reply” and “respond” need “to”, and you “notify” a person, not an invoice.
content.stem: 122.Please _____ the attached invoice carefully and let us know if you have any questions about the charges.

content.explanation.0: Why: “By the time … next spring” refers to an action completed before a future point, so the future perfect “will have hired” is needed.
content.stem: 123.By the time the new factory in Monterrey opens next spring, the company _____ more than two hundred workers.

content.explanation.0: Why: The figures are the things being sent, and “yesterday” requires the past, so the past passive “were sent” is correct.
content.stem: 124.The quarterly sales figures _____ to all regional managers yesterday afternoon, along with the new targets.

content.explanation.0: Why: "Remain open" describes a continuing situation, so "until" marks when it ends. "By" is the trap: it gives a deadline for a completed action ("finish by the end of October"), not the end point of an ongoing state.
content.stem: 125.The museum’s special exhibition on maritime trade will remain open _____ the end of October.

content.explanation.0: Why: The verb “consider” is followed by a gerund, so “moving” is correct.
content.stem: 126.The organizing committee is considering _____ the annual logistics conference to a larger venue in Singapore.

content.explanation.0: Why: A machine that has been repaired is now running "flawlessly" (without any problems). "Reluctantly" describes a person's attitude, and "tightly" and "considerably" do not describe how a machine operates.
content.stem: 127.Assembly Line 2 has been running _____ since the technicians replaced its faulty sensors last week.

content.explanation.0: Why: The collocation is “eligible for” (meeting the conditions for something); “capable” takes “of”, and “responsible” and “reliable” do not fit the meaning.
content.stem: 128.Online orders placed before noon are _____ for same-day delivery to addresses within the city limits.

content.explanation.0: Why: The revision is the natural result of the request, so “accordingly” (= as a result) fits; “nevertheless” would signal a contrast.
content.stem: 129.The client requested several changes to the floor plan; _____ , the architects revised the drawings within a week.

content.explanation.0: Why: A checkout process that customers find easy to understand and use is "intuitive." "Exhaustive" (thorough, complete), "cooperative" (willing to help) and "tentative" (not certain) do not describe how easy a process is to use.
content.stem: 130.The survey results show that most customers find the new online checkout process much more _____ than the old one.

content.explanation.0: Why: The sentence describes a condition (pieces missing) and what to do in that case, so “If” is correct; “Unless” reverses the meaning and “Although” signals contrast.

Tenants are reminded that smoking is not permitted in the lobby.
The tower was completed more than thirty years ago.

Whether she can end her contract early
Whether a promotional price will still apply
Whether Corvanta has a store near her office

content.stem: 185.What is suggested about Alcántara Travel?

It will get a personal account manager.
It holds video calls with airline partners.
It has used Corvanta’s services for years.

To ask for a copy of an invoice
To order more chairs for an event

content.stem: 189.What is suggested about Ms. Kahale’s complaint about the linens?

content.text.0: It was submitted after the deadline.
It meets the conditions for a refund.

To introduce a new facilities manager

At a charging point in the building

content.explanation.0: Why: The fall in costs is a result of the early installation, so “consequently” is correct; “nevertheless” would wrongly signal a contrast between two positive facts.
content.stem: 101.The factory’s new packaging line was installed ahead of schedule; _____ , production costs fell by nearly 8 percent in the first month.

content.explanation.0: Why: Rising fuel prices are the reason for the higher charges, so “Due to” fits; “In spite of” would illogically present the price rise as an obstacle to raising charges.
content.stem: 102._____ rising fuel prices, Vandermeer Logistics has raised its delivery charges for the first time in four years.

content.explanation.0: Why: Customers who feel an emotion are described with the -ed participle, so “disappointed” is correct; “disappointing” would describe the thing that causes the feeling, such as the sale.
content.stem: 103.Several _____ customers wrote to the store manager after the weekend sale ended earlier than advertised.

content.explanation.0: Why: The clause after the gap is complete and describes a place (the harbor), so the relative adverb “where” is needed; “which” would require a missing subject or object in the clause.
content.stem: 104.The walking tour includes a stop at the old harbor, _____ visitors can sample fresh seafood from local vendors.

content.explanation.0: Why: An adverb is needed to modify the passive verb “was adopted”, so “successfully” is correct; “successful” is an adjective and cannot modify a verb.
content.stem: 105.The new staff scheduling software was _____ adopted by all twelve of the chain’s restaurants within a month.

content.explanation.0: Why: A receipt is needed to return goods for a “refund or exchange”, which is the standard collocation; a “discount” or “deposit” is not something a customer obtains by returning merchandise.
content.stem: 106.Please keep your original receipt, as it is required for any _____ or exchange of merchandise.

content.explanation.0: Why: The reflexive pronoun “herself” is used for emphasis to mean that Ms. Albescu does the review personally; “her” and “hers” cannot stand alone after the object here.
content.stem: 107.Ms. Albescu prefers to review the quarterly sales figures _____ before presenting them to the board of directors.

content.explanation.0: Why: “By the time … opens next spring” refers to an action completed before a future point, so the future perfect “will have hired” is required; “had hired” refers to the past.
content.stem: 108.By the time the new assembly plant opens next spring, the company _____ more than 300 additional workers.

content.explanation.0: Why: After “The” and before “of”, a noun is required, so “construction” is correct; the other choices are a verb, an adjective and a participle.
content.stem: 109.The _____ of the new visitor center has been postponed until the city approves the revised building plans.

content.explanation.0: Why: The singular noun “employee” and singular verb pattern require “Every”; “All”, “Most” and “Many” must be followed by a plural noun such as “employees”.
content.stem: 110._____ employee attending the safety seminar at the pharmaceutical plant must sign in at the front desk.

content.explanation.0: Why: “From … until …” marks the start and end of a period, so “from” is correct; “since” is used with a past starting point and a perfect tense.
content.stem: 111.The Riverside Farmers Market is open every Saturday _____ 7:00 A.M. until noon from May through October.

content.explanation.0: Why: The subject is “Each”, which is singular, so “is” is required; “are” is the trap that agrees with the nearby plural noun “cars”.
content.stem: 112.Each of the rental cars at our airport locations _____ inspected for damage before it is released to a customer.

content.explanation.0: Why: One “presents” identification when asked to show it, so “present” fits; “express”, “perform” and “attend” do not collocate with “a photo ID”.
content.stem: 113.Visitors to the Kestrel Pharmaceuticals research laboratory must _____ a valid photo ID at the security desk.

content.explanation.0: Why: The fitness room is on the floor over the lobby, so “above” is correct; “between” would need two reference points and “among” needs a group.
content.stem: 114.The new staff fitness room is located directly _____ the main lobby, on the second floor of the building.

content.explanation.0: Why: After “aims to”, a base-form verb that can take the object “the time” is required, so “shorten” is correct; the other choices are an adjective, an adverb and a noun.
content.stem: 115.The company’s new return policy aims to _____ the time required to process customer refunds.

content.explanation.0: Why: A conjunction is needed before the clause “Ms. Oyelaran is attending …”, and “while” shows the two events happen at the same time; “during” and “despite” are prepositions and cannot introduce a clause.
content.stem: 116.Mr. Vaillancourt will lead the factory tour _____ Ms. Oyelaran is attending the trade fair in Frankfurt.

content.explanation.0: Why: An adjective is needed to describe the noun “design”, so “attractive” is correct; “attractively” is an adverb and “attract” is a verb.
content.stem: 117.Customers have praised the new line of kitchen appliances for its _____ design and low energy use.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Recommend” is followed by a gerund when there is no personal object, so “making” is correct; “recommends to make” is a common learner error.
content.stem: 118.The travel agency recommends _____ hotel reservations at least two months in advance during the festival season.

content.explanation.0: Why: The word “also” shows the business show will be added to the news program, so “In addition to” is correct; “As long as” is a conjunction and cannot come before a noun phrase.
content.stem: 119._____ its popular morning news program, Channel 9 will also begin broadcasting a weekly business show in March.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Highly recommended” is the fixed collocation meaning strongly advised; “deeply”, “tightly” and “heavily” do not combine with “recommended”.
content.stem: 120.Tickets for the Lakeshore Food Festival are expected to sell out quickly, so early booking is _____ recommended.

content.explanation.0: Why: “A thorough knowledge” means a complete and detailed knowledge, which is the natural collocation; “lengthy” describes duration and “generous” describes amounts or people.
content.stem: 121.Applicants for the parts manager position should have a _____ knowledge of automotive parts and accessories.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Typically” (= usually) fits a general statement about how soon orders are ready. “Briefly” describes duration (ready briefly?), and “evenly” and “mutually” do not collocate with “ready for pickup.”
content.stem: 122.Orders placed through our website are _____ ready for pickup within two hours of confirmation.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Ever since it first opened in 2019” describes a situation continuing up to now, so the present perfect “has worked” is required. Trap: “had worked” (past perfect) needs a later past reference point, which the sentence does not have.
content.stem: 123.Ms. Khoury _____ as head chef at the Marigold Bistro ever since it first opened in 2019.

content.explanation.0: Why: The main clause uses “would begin”, so the if-clause needs the simple past “arrived” (second conditional); “had arrived” would require “would have begun”.
content.stem: 124.If the shipment of spare parts _____ by Friday, the repair work on the delivery trucks would begin on Monday.

content.explanation.0: Why: “Thoroughly inspected” (= checked carefully and completely) is the natural collocation. “Highly” goes with adjectives like “recommended,” “greatly” with verbs of change like “improved,” and “widely” with “used” or “known.”
content.stem: 125.All returned merchandise is _____ inspected before it is placed back on the store shelves.

content.explanation.0: Why: The café is offered during the period of the closure, so “in the meantime” is correct; “otherwise” would mean “if the restaurant does not close”, which is illogical.
content.stem: 126.The hotel’s rooftop restaurant will close for renovations in July; _____ , guests may enjoy breakfast in the lobby café.

content.explanation.0: Why: A comparative (“more … than”) is intensified with “considerably,” “much,” or “far.” Trap: “very more” is a common learner error — “very” cannot modify a comparative; “such” and “so” do not work before “more” here.
content.stem: 127.The Alderton plant produced _____ more vehicles last quarter than any other factory in the region.

content.explanation.0: Why: A deadline for a one-time action (“submit”) takes “by.” Trap: “until” is used for a continuing state (“The office is open until Wednesday”); “within” needs a period of time, and “since” needs a perfect tense.
content.stem: 128.Staff members who wish to attend the training workshop should submit their registration forms _____ Wednesday, 4 March.

content.explanation.0: Why: The gap is followed by a noun phrase (“forecasts of heavy rain”), so a preposition is needed; “in light of” (= because of) gives the reason. “Even though,” “provided that” and “so that” are conjunctions and must be followed by a clause.
content.stem: 129.The festival organizers decided to move the concert indoors _____ forecasts of heavy rain for the weekend.

content.explanation.0: Why: Results (things) are “distributed to” people. Trap: “informed” and “notified” take a person as their object (“department heads will be informed of the results”), so “the results will be informed” is wrong; “acquainted” also needs a person.
content.stem: 130.The results of the customer satisfaction survey will be _____ to all department heads once the analysis is complete.

content.explanation.0: Why: The employees receive the request, so the passive “are asked” is needed; “have asked” is active and would mean the employees made the request.
content.stem: 131.

content.explanation.0: Why: The pattern “between 7:00 A.M. and 10:00 P.M.” is completed by “and”, so “between” is correct; “from” would need “to” or “until”.
content.stem: 132.

content.explanation.0: Why: “This” refers back to the closing of the north garage described in the first paragraph, so “closure” is correct; nothing in the notice mentions a promotion or a delivery.
content.stem: 133.

content.explanation.0: Why: After admitting the closure “may cause some inconvenience,” the notice justifies it — “however” signals that contrast. B contradicts the first paragraph (staff must use the Carver Street lot; the south garage is for customers), C has the wrong time (the work has not started), and D is never supported by the notice.

content.text.0: The work is necessary, however, to keep the garage safe for everyone.

For this reason, the Easter weekend sale has been postponed until May.

content.explanation.0: Why: The relative pronoun refers to people (visitors) and acts as the subject of “want”, so “who” is correct; “which” is used for things.

content.explanation.0: Why: An adjective is needed before the noun “explanations”, so the participle adjective “detailed” is correct; “detail” and “details” are nouns.

Baskets are provided, and the fruit is sold by weight at the farm shop.
The greenhouse part of the tour is offered only to school groups.
Strawberries are usually in season on the farm from April to May.

content.explanation.0: Why: The web page gives current general information in the present tense (“Tickets cost”, “Tours depart”), so the simple present “advise” is correct; the past forms do not fit an ongoing recommendation.
content.stem: 138.

content.explanation.0: Why: After the article “a” and before “of”, a noun is required, so “reduction” is correct; “reduce” is a verb and “reduced” is a participle.
content.stem: 139.

content.explanation.0: Why: “About” is used before a number to mean approximately, so “takes about 45 minutes” is correct; “much”, “very” and “quite” cannot modify a number in this way.
content.stem: 140.

content.explanation.0: Why: The sentence continues the idea of relaxing in the lounge while the 45-minute inspection is done. content.stem: 141.

content.text.0: Our technicians will call you when the car is ready to collect the next day.
Please note that the lounge is currently closed for renovation.
A courtesy car can be provided while your vehicle is with us.
Free coffee and Wi-Fi are available while you wait.

content.explanation.0: Why: The repairs are found by the technicians, so the reduced passive “identified” (= that are identified) is correct; “identifying” would mean the repairs do the identifying.
content.stem: 142.

content.explanation.0: Why: The gap is joined by “and” to the participle “plugged in”, so the parallel past participle “connected” is required.
content.stem: 143.

content.explanation.0: Why: An adverb is needed to describe how to press, so “firmly” is correct; “firm” and “firmer” are adjectives.

content.explanation.0: Why: The sentence explains how the labels are linked to the inventory system mentioned in the previous sentence, so “To do this” is correct; “In contrast” and “Even so” wrongly signal opposition.

content.explanation.0: Why: After the green check mark for a successful link, the instructions logically explain what to do if the link fails. To advertise a café on a ferry

To inform passengers about changes to a service

content.explanation.0: Why: The notice says drivers are “strongly encouraged to reserve space in advance”; commuter passes and the upper deck are mentioned for other reasons.

content.explanation.0: Why: She complains that the hot breakfast dishes ran out and were not replaced; she gave check-in the highest rating.
content.stem: 154.What does Ms. Solberg want the hotel to improve?

content.text.0: The supply of food in the morning
The speed of the check-in process
The hours of the fitness center

content.explanation.0: Why: The page explains how listeners can submit stories for Community Voices; the studio is mentioned only as the place where selected stories are recorded.

To advertise a recording studio for rent
To invite listeners to send in stories
To recruit volunteers to produce a program

content.explanation.0: Why: The station replies “only to those people whose stories are selected”, so many submissions get no answer; summaries must be no more than 300 words and are sent through a form.

content.stem: 157.What will contributors who cannot visit the studio receive?

content.stem: 159.What are users instructed to do before applying the product?

content.text.0: Measure the temperature of the soil

content.explanation.0: Why: A gardening helpline is open Monday to Friday; the label says the product must not freeze and that one bottle makes up to 200 liters.

content.text.0: Advice is available by telephone on weekdays.

The product is suitable only for vegetables.

content.explanation.0: Why: The review says she “closed her small lunch counter at the Eastgate Market”, so she previously ran a smaller business; she no longer works at the market.

content.explanation.0: Why: He calls the slow-cooked chicken with apricots “the highlight of the meal”; the vegetable platter is described only as generous, and the desserts were ordinary.
content.stem: 162.What did the reviewer enjoy most?

content.explanation.0: Why: The restaurant opens at 5:00 P.M., so it does not serve lunch; being open Tuesday through Sunday, prices up to $24 and the busy Friday visit are all stated.
content.stem: 163.What is NOT indicated about Saffron & Salt?

content.stem: 164.What problem is being discussed?

content.text.0: A supplier sent the wrong labels.
A machine is not working properly.
A shipment was damaged in transit.

content.explanation.0: Why: Ms. Nwosu says the order “is supposed to go out first thing tomorrow”; it will be moved to Line 1, not Line 3.
content.stem: 165.What is suggested about the Merriton order?

content.text.0: It has been canceled by the customer.
It will be produced on Line 3.
It is scheduled to be shipped the next day.
It is smaller than the Holloway order.

content.explanation.0: Why: After learning that moving the job to Line 1 would only delay an order that is not urgent, she accepts Mr. Pereira’s plan; she does not choose to wait for Line 3 to be repaired.
content.stem: 166.At 2:13 P.M., what does Ms. Nwosu mean when she writes, “Then let’s go with that”?

content.text.0: She wants the Holloway order shipped first.
She will contact the supplier herself.
She agrees to wait for the repair.

content.explanation.0: Why: Asked to tell the warehouse that the pallets will be late, she replies “I’ll message them now”; the roller is being obtained by the technician.
content.stem: 167.What will Ms. Rautio most likely do next?

content.text.0: Notify the warehouse of a delay

content.explanation.0: Why: The memo explains when and how the department will move into the new laboratory building; the construction is already complete.
content.stem: 168.What is the purpose of the memo?

content.text.0: To provide information about a relocation
To describe a new research project
To introduce a new facilities manager
To request help with a construction project

content.explanation.0: Why: It will stay where it is because “its new testing equipment has not yet been delivered”; the analytical chemistry team moves first.
content.stem: 169.What is indicated about the quality control laboratory?

It is already on the west side of the campus.
It is waiting for equipment to arrive.
It will close permanently next month.

content.explanation.0: Why: Staff cannot enter “until their security badges have been updated,” and badges “can be updated at the reception desk in the main building.” Trap: team leaders receive a moving schedule; staff do not submit one.
content.stem: 170.What must staff do before they can enter the new building?

content.text.0: Stop by the reception desk in the main building
Collect keys from their team leader

content.explanation.0: Why: The sentence explains the colored stickers mentioned just before position [3], and the following sentence about unlabeled items continues the same topic.
content.stem: 171.In which of the positions marked [1] , [2] , [3] , and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “Each team has been assigned a different color.”

content.explanation.0: Why: The release announces a new battery manufacturing plant; new models and the college are mentioned only as related details.
content.stem: 172.What is the press release mainly about?

content.text.0: The launch of a new vehicle model
The construction of a new production facility
The appointment of a company executive
